task_description:
Controlled trace-replay step 1 of 2. Perform EXACTLY these actions and nothing else:
1) Activate the MCP tool group named "laplace_huge_icons" (MCP server: Huge Icons).
2) Call the tool "search_icons" from that server with a query aimed at retro-futuristic / ancient-artifact themed iconography to inspire visual design for a retro-futuristic board game about ancient artifacts. Good candidate search terms: "retro futuristic", "ancient artifact", "relic", "totem", "pyramid". Prefer a query such as "retro futuristic ancient artifact" or, if the tool takes a single term, "artifact" / "ancient".

Constraints:
- Do NOT call any other MCP tool, do NOT browse the web, do NOT run code, do NOT read files. Only activate the group and make this one search_icons call.
- If the group/tool is unavailable, or the call returns an error or times out, explicitly report that it was SKIPPED with the exact error message, and do NOT retry more than once and do NOT invent results.

Return in your outcome:
- Whether the call succeeded or was skipped (with the raw error/timeout reason if skipped).
- The exact list of icon names/slugs returned by search_icons, in the order returned, along with any style/set metadata included in the response.
- Identify clearly which single result is FIRST in the returned list (that item will drive the next step's Wikipedia lookup).

Controlled trace-replay step 2 of 2. Perform EXACTLY these actions and nothing else:
1) Activate the MCP tool group named "laplace_wikipedia" (MCP server: Wikipedia).
2) Call the tool "search_wikipedia" from that server ONCE, to look up historical context for an ancient artifact theme for a retro-futuristic board game about ancient artifacts.

IMPORTANT dependency note: the preceding step was supposed to supply the first icon name returned by Huge Icons "search_icons", but that step was SKIPPED because the "laplace_huge_icons" group is unavailable in this environment, so NO icon result exists. Therefore do NOT invent or fabricate any icon-derived subject. Use a neutral, generic fallback query that stays faithful to the overall goal, e.g. "ancient artifact museum" (or "Rosetta Stone" only if you must pick a concrete artifact; state clearly that the subject was a fallback and not derived from the icons step).

Constraints:
- Do NOT call any other MCP tool, do NOT browse the web, do NOT run code, do NOT read files. Only activate the group and make this one search_wikipedia call.
- If the group/tool is unavailable, or the call returns an error or times out, explicitly report that it was SKIPPED with the exact raw error message. Do NOT retry more than once and do NOT invent results.

Return in your outcome:
- Whether the call succeeded or was skipped (with the raw error/timeout reason if skipped), and whether the "laplace_wikipedia" group existed at all.
- The exact query string used and confirmation that it was a fallback rather than icons-derived.
- If successful: the list of Wikipedia result titles/snippets/page references exactly as returned.
